notes: lowGround uses fixed Chennai breakpoints: 1.0 at or below 2 m, 0 at or above 20 m
builtUp = 60% of built-up land use coverage plus measured building footprint coverage of the cell
haz[year] stores only the two hazard terms (0-60) so the app can rescore a cell with wetlands restored
depth[year] is modelled from the published zone plus a terrain hollow term; measured points override Today
sea, rivers, lakes and marsh cells carry mask = 1 and no score
wet[cell] = modelled share of hazard removed if the surrounding wetlands were restored (0-100)
pop[cell] = footprint/85 m2 * 3.51 persons (Census 2011 TN) — challenge 4.4 exposure estimate
bldc[cell] = building footprint count; roadd[cell] = metres of mapped road
pop[cell] = footprint/85 m2 * 3.51 persons (Census 2011 TN) — challenge 4.4 exposure estimate
bldc[cell] = building footprint count; roadd[cell] = metres of mapped road
crit[cell] = critical facilities: hospital, clinic, doctors, school, college, university, kindergarten, police, fire_station, shelter, community_centre
LH[cell] = landslide susceptibility 0-100 from DEM slope (Zevenbergen-Thorne): 0 below 3°, 100 above 15° — PS 1.1 second hazard layer

popMeta.anchor: Census of India 2011, Tamil Nadu average household size (3.51)
popMeta.limit: An occupancy model, not a census count of buildings. Reads as population present on an average day.

critMeta.basis: OpenStreetMap points of interest, Protomaps pois layer

mhMeta.basis: MCDM weighted overlay of the flood hazard term (packed HAZ+year), landslide susceptibility from DEM slope (LH), and built exposure (EXPO)
mhMeta.formula: MH = 10 * (0.45*hazard + 0.40*landslide + 0.15*exposure), computed per cell in the browser for every year

susceptibility.method: Zevenbergen-Thorne slope on the baked elevation grid

mhMeta.honesty: Chennai is coastal plain: landslide susceptibility is ~0 nearly everywhere. The layer proves the multi-hazard framework and re-targets to hilly cities unchanged.
